topic: automated program repair; fault localization; neural repair; robustness to code transformations
status: bounded synthesis of four cross-period audits (including two earlier frame papers); testable evaluation hypothesis, not pooled effect or field prevalence
claim: APR results in this slice depend on pipeline conditions that are often scored separately: fault localization, test-oracle strength, patch correctness definition, and code representation. A search-based repair study finds GenProg performance changes with fault-space accuracy; MUFIN reports gains over a matched neural baseline while assuming perfect fault localization; a separate 11-model study reports large drops on semantics-preserving transformed Defects4J. Thus a single repair score does not identify whether a method generalizes end to end. This does not invalidate component studies: oracle localization is a legitimate control when the claim is specifically about patch generation.
positive_evidence: The fault-space study reports failure rates as high as 60% when the real fix location is ranked below 10, despite the correct patch remaining in the search space.
MUFIN improves on its matched baseline from 16 to 28 correct Defects4J fixes and from 43 to 62 plausible fixes under perfect fault localization.
On Defects4J-Trans, 11 LLMs show average drops of 49.48% in correct fixes and 42.90% in plausible fixes relative to original Defects4J.
counterevidence: Perfect fault localization in MUFIN is an explicit experimental control to isolate patch generation, not an invalid design for that narrower question.
The transformed benchmark is a particular set of single-function Java transformations; results may not generalize to other languages, transformations, datasets, or stronger systems.
Plausible test-passing patches and manually judged equivalence to the historical developer patch are useful but distinct correctness measures.
falsifiable_test: Across several repositories and languages, factorially vary fault-localization quality, test-suite strength, and semantics-preserving source transformations while holding patch generator and compute fixed. Report compilation, test plausibility, independent semantic correctness, regression safety, and end-to-end wall-clock cost separately. The hypothesis weakens if method rankings and success remain stable across these upstream conditions.
limitations: Evidence spans different generations of APR and incompatible benchmarks; the outcomes are not pooled. Only one source here studies LLM robustness transformations, and the sample cannot estimate how common these dependencies are across APR literature.

topic: formal program verification; specification quality; proof-producing agents
status: bounded synthesis of three cross-period full-text audits; evaluation-design hypothesis, not a claim that formal proofs are unreliable
claim: A machine-checked proof establishes that an implementation satisfies the formal statement under the logic and assumptions; it does not by itself establish that the formal statement captures the intended requirement. In the 2026 CLEVER study, authors flag issues in 80 of 161 reference problems and report 98.1% end-to-end success after removing four benchmark-issue entries (95.7% when retaining them over two runs). By contrast, ownership-refinement work proves soundness of a stated type system, and Yogar-CBMC's guarantee is explicitly bounded by loop unwinding. These evidence types should be reported separately: proof validity, specification adequacy, assumptions/bounds, and behavior on fresh tasks.
positive_evidence: CLEVER analysis identifies ambiguities and defects in problem specifications; downstream proof generation exposes issues missed by isomorphism checks.
Ownership-refinement types provide a formal soundness theorem and an implemented verifier on nested-array examples.
Yogar-CBMC gives a formal soundness/completeness guarantee relative to the chosen bounded unwinding depth and evaluates 1,047 concurrency programs.
counterevidence: Machine-checked proof is strong evidence for the formal proposition and should not be discounted merely because natural-language intent can be ambiguous.

The CLEVER paper reports both the broader 95.7% figure and the conditional 98.1% figure, making the exclusion visible; its task-level benchmark issues do not imply that all proof benchmarks are defective.
The type-system and bounded-model-checking guarantees have explicitly delimited assumptions; they are not examples of unsupported empirical claims.
falsifiable_test: Create fresh verification tasks with independently adjudicated natural-language intent, machine-checkable formal specifications, and seeded specification/benchmark defects. Report proof-check success, intent preservation, issue-detection sensitivity, assumptions/bounds, and downstream behavior separately. The hypothesis weakens if raw proof acceptance predicts intent-correct behavior as well as independent specification adjudication on held-out tasks.
limitations: Three papers cover different notions of verification and cannot establish a universal benchmark-quality problem. The proposed fresh benchmark was not implemented in this literature audit.

topic: literature retrieval and audit methodology; program repair and verification taxonomy
status: audit of the fixed 12-key random frame cell; screening-quality observation, not prevalence estimate outside this frame
claim: The fixed random frame label `program_repair_verification` bundles different research objects and endpoints. The 12 sampled keys include automated program repair/search-prior work, formal verification/type systems, model-based testing, a functional-safety platform description, quantum programming semantics, and one arXiv record for an edited proceedings volume rather than a standalone paper. Even within repair, modeled attempts, plausible test-passing patches, manually judged patch equivalence, and transformation robustness are not interchangeable outcomes. The screen is useful for retrieval, but its label should not be read as a coherent subfield or a single trend.
positive_evidence: The 2013 repair-model paper measures mined AST-change distributions and theoretically modeled search attempts, while the 2023 MUFIN paper measures plausible and manually judged repairs under oracle localization.
The 2014 quantum-language paper develops QGCL semantics; the 2014 ASDSpec paper studies model-based testing; the 2017/2026 items include bounded verification and proof-producing agents.
The sampled arXiv:1506.03250 record has no attached PDF and describes the 99-page EPTCS proceedings volume; the volume contains six distinct papers selected from 15 submissions.
counterevidence: Formal verification and language semantics can legitimately be adjacent to a broad program-repair/verification opportunity screen; this audit does not show that the umbrella category is useless.
A broad discovery screen may intentionally favor recall over precise taxonomy; labels can be refined during full-text screening rather than used as final scientific classes.

sources.sections: arXiv record; official EPTCS proceedings cover, preface, and contents

falsifiable_test: On a new stratified sample of at least 100 records from this retrieval label, have two independent reviewers assign multi-label research-object classes and evidence-endpoint types, recording proceedings/survey/software-record anomalies. Compute agreement and per-label precision/recall against the original screen; then compare pooled analyses with analyses stratified by object/outcome. The heterogeneity concern weakens if agreement is high and conclusions remain stable under properly stratified outcomes.
limitations: Only the fixed 12-key sample cell was checked; labels are heuristic and this is not a random draw from all arXiv-CS records under a gold-standard taxonomy. One proceedings volume received only front matter/contents review, and its six constituent papers are not individually represented as full-text audits.
